current_status.from: Active as of 2026-09-23; Ordinance 2026-38 (six-month moratorium, public hearing closed 6:30 p.m. with no comment, adopted 7-0 the same evening on 2026-04-13) remains in effect through its stated October 10, 2026 expiration. On 2026-09-10, Tallmadge City Council's Planning & Zoning Committee opened a first reading of Ordinance 2026-74, which would extend the moratorium for an additional 12 months effective 2026-10-13 (i.e., immediately upon the current moratorium's expiration), following a public hearing scheduled for 2026-10-08. As of this pass Ordinance 2026-74 has not been adopted: the filed ordinance text shows blank 'Passed,' vote-tally, and readings fields, and reporting on the September 10 committee session confirms 'The ordinance did not receive a vote tonight and remains at first reading while staff and the law department continue review.' A regional real-estate industry brief (Akron Cleveland Association of Realtors, 'Local Lineup,' 2026-09-10) characterized the item as already 'extended,' but the underlying agenda and ordinance documents show it is still pending as of 2026-09-23.

evidence.quote:
SECTION 1. That Council hereby extends the moratorium, for twelve months effective October 13, 2026, that the City

shall not accept, process, or approve any new applications or issue any new permits, licenses, variances, or any zoning

applications from or for data centers within the City of Tallmadge.

SECTION 2. The moratorium shall be in effect for a period of twelve months from the effective date of this ordinance

or until changes are enacted to amend the Codified Ordinances of the City of Tallmadge to address data centers or until

Council approves legislation explicitly revoking this moratorium, whichever occurs first. Council reserves the right to

extend this moratorium if reasonable and necessary.

decisions.notes: Adoption established; posted text does not establish mayoral approval or exclude subsequent action. No fixed expiry asserted.
